subject: Launch stitch: handoff, acceptance criteria & escalation paths
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@cardiotech.io>
Date: 2026-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Launch stitch: handoff, acceptance criteria & escalation paths

Hi team —

Thanks for the quick close last week. CardioTech signed yesterday and asked for a tight go-live in 8 weeks (targeting 2026-08-24). Below is the context and the handoff asks so CS / Implementation can scope properly.

Quick summary
- Account: CardioTech Inc. (B2B med-dev analytics).
- Committed SKU: Dedicated-small (2x A100 equivalent), Redwood API + 30-day evaluation window for embeddings throughput.
- Monthly committed spend: $26k.
- Primary contacts: Elaine Park (product lead), Samir Rao (procurement).

Key constraints & asks for CS
1) Security: CardioTech requires SOC2 evidence and an IP allowlist for access to the private staging cluster.
2) Data residency: logs retained in us-west region only for 90 days.
3) Latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms for 512-token generative calls; they will run heavy burst windows (simulated load on Tuesdays).
4) Integration: they want an event-based webhook to their ingestion service (POST /ingest) and high-throughput embeddings for similarity search.

Immediate deliverables we promised
- Draft SOW with timeline (attached: CardioTech_SOW_v0.3.pdf).
- Discovery notes + sample prompts (attached).
- Internal canary cadence + rollback plan.

Risks and escalation paths
- Risk: their legal may request a non-standard indemnity clause; Ben will own legal loop but CS should flag if the SOW schedule needs pushing.
- Escalation: any production-impacting regression during canary -> page on-call infra (Vivek) and notify Elaine + Ben.

Owner suggestions (please confirm):
- Implementation lead: Olga Petrov (if available)
- Technical QA / performance lead: Vivek Kulkarni
- Customer-facing CS: Tessa Morgan

Next actions
- Olga: propose a 6-week sprint plan and resourcing (who owns staging, who runs canary). Due: EOD 2026-06-29.
- Tessa: schedule kickoff with CardioTech for week of 2026-07-06.
- Ben: push SOW to DocuSign after Olga confirms timeline.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0191

Attachments: CardioTech_SOW_v0.3.pdf, discovery-notes-cardio-20260624.xlsx
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@cardiotech.io>
Date: 2026-06-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch stitch: handoff, acceptance criteria & escalation paths

Thanks Ben — good summary. I'm available to lead but will need a full-time engineer for the first three sprints to handle kernel selection and the private staging setup. I've sketched a high-level sprint plan below.

High-level 6-week sprint plan
- Week 0 (2026-07-06): Kickoff + environment access, confirm security checklist (SOC2 docs + IP allowlist).
- Week 1-2: Private staging deployment, quantization/throughput tuning for embeddings, baseline perf tests.
- Week 3-4: Integration with CardioTech ingestion webhook + run simulated burst tests (Tuesday windows).
- Week 5: Canary with 10% traffic and run acceptance prompts; regressions -> immediate rollback per plan.
- Week 6: Production cutover and 30-day observation window.

Open questions for CardioTech (Elaine/Samir)
- Can they provide the webhook auth scheme (HMAC secret) and a non-prod endpoint by 2026-07-08?
- For logs retention, confirm whether 90-day S3 lifecycle is sufficient vs. dedicated index.

I'll draft a staffing ask for Eng and QA. Ben, can you confirm whether we have permission to run the simulated Tuesday bursts for the dedicated pool (bursts may require temporary autoscale increase)? If not, we'll need an alternate window.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@cardiotech.io>, Samir Rao <samir@cardiotech.io>
Date: 2026-06-28T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch stitch: handoff, acceptance criteria & escalation paths

Perfect — I'll take the customer kickoff and own success criteria. Proposed kickoff agenda (30 min):
- Introductions and roles (5m)
- High-level timeline & milestones (5m)
- Security checklist items we need from CardioTech (10m)
- Integration points: webhook and embeddings (5m)
- Next steps and immediate asks (5m)

Availability: 2026-07-06, 2026-07-07 between 10a–2p PT. Elaine, what works?

Also flagged in the HubSpot deal that procurement may ask for a 60-day invoice term; Ben, is that approved? If not, I'll note as a finance ask.

Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.com
From: Elaine Park <elaine@cardiotech.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Rao <samir@cardiotech.io>
Date: 2026-06-28T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch stitch: handoff, acceptance criteria & escalation paths

Thanks all — excited to get started. 2026-07-06 at 10:30a PT works for the kickoff. A couple quick items from our side:
- We will send the non-prod webhook endpoint + HMAC secret by 2026-07-02.
- Procurement (Samir) confirms they want 60-day invoice terms; we can accept if Redwood adds a small payment schedule clause to the SOW to protect both sides.
- For the simulated Tuesday bursts, we can run a replay exercise in staging first week of August; prefer not to stress production during initial 30 days.

Elaine Park
Head of Product | CardioTech Inc.
elaine@cardiotech.io | +1 650-555-0142
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine@cardiotech.io>
Date: 2026-06-29T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch stitch: handoff, acceptance criteria & escalation paths

Looping back after reviewing the SOW and discovery notes. Technical notes / blockers:
- Quantization profile: for their throughput targets we should use int8-kernel set A (reduced mem) — estimate a 28% token-cost reduction but needs validation on their prompt set.
- Autoscale: we can allow controlled bursts but need procurement approval for a temporary capacity buffer (Ben: please confirm).
- IP allowlist: Ops needs the exact CIDR ranges from CardioTech before we can enable access to the private staging cluster.

I'll pair with Olga on the perf tests next Tuesday to run baseline runs against the sample prompts in discovery-notes-cardio-20260624.xlsx.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Staff Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
